_comment: Confirmed 1.8V-core MOS corner-model file list for the sky130A PDK
checkout pinned in sim/gm-id-characterization/pdk.json (open_pdks
c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b). This is the artifact that
closes issue #6's 'corner-grid confirmation' scope item and is the
pointer target for spec/target-spec.md Section 1's 'Corner grid' row.
Verified 2026-09-08 by directly grepping every
libs.tech/ngspice/corners/<corner>.spice file in the pinned checkout
for its nfet_01v8/pfet_01v8 .include lines (excluding the mismatch and
ESD-device .include lines, which are separate concerns not swept by
this experiment). Each entry below is the literal path resolved from
that checkout, relative to $PDK_ROOT/sky130A/.
sky130-bandgap's own ratified corner set (tt, ff, ss, fs, sf) is the
same *shape* of grid, but that sibling's ratified spec runs its
devices at 3.3V using the I/O-tolerant flavor -- this file is the
1.8V-core-specific confirmation porting-plan.md Section 4 asked for,
not a copy of that sibling's file names.
Naming convention (SkyWater sky130, standard across the PDK): tt =
typical-typical, ff = fast-fast, ss = slow-slow, fs = fast-NMOS/
slow-PMOS, sf = slow-NMOS/fast-PMOS. This experiment does not itself
depend on that mnemonic being correct in either direction -- each
corner's nfet_01v8 and pfet_01v8 data is measured and reported on its
own terms (see records/), not inferred from the corner's name.
note_on_temperature_and_supply: Process corner (this file) and simulation temperature are orthogonal in sky130's ngspice deck convention -- temperature is a `.temp` analysis setting, not a separate model file. This experiment's PVT grid is therefore process (5, this file) x temperature (3: -40C/27C/125C, matching spec/target-spec.md Section 1's Operating temperature row). Supply voltage is not a separate swept axis for this bare-device study: VDS is the study's own representative fixed bias (see README.md), not a node tied to a VDD net the way a full-circuit testbench's PSRR/line-regulation bench would sweep VIN -- there is no 'supply corner' for a two-terminal-bias device sweep, so this experiment does not manufacture one.
